c.h: This guide describes the most effective methods to train the Thieving skill up to level 120. Thieving is a support skill that involves using techniques such as pickpocketing, coshing and lock picking to steal items and to gain access to restricted areas. As players level up the Thieving skill, they gain the ability to steal from NPCs and scenery objects, which award greater amounts of experience when they are successfully stolen from. Levelling up Thieving also decreases the chance of failing Thieving activities where there is a chance of being unsuccessful. The experience rate estimates in this guide do not incorporate the use of any experience-boosting items or bonus experience. For pickpocketing methods, success chance depends on the player's Thieving level, the target's level requirement, success chance boosts, and the number of consecutive pickpockets made from the same target. Actual experience rates and AFK time therefore vary depending on the player's setup and how often they refresh or change targets.

The Thieving success chance calculator can be used to work out your success rate while Thieving based on your level and the boosts available to you.

Pickpocketing is a low-intensity training method in which the player automatically repeats the pickpocket action until they are caught, their inventory becomes full, or they stop the action. Success chance is based on the player's Thieving level compared with the target's level requirement, with an opening success boost for a limited number of pickpockets. After those boosted pickpockets, the success chance gradually falls until the player is caught or the pickpocketing chain is reset. Changing target or refreshing Crystal Mask resets the chain.

The useful equipment table above lists the main success chance, stun avoidance, healing, and inventory-management items for pickpocketing. These boosts mainly increase the time before a player needs to change or refresh targets. The Thieving chance calculator can be used to check success chance, AFK duration, experience, and profit for a specific setup.

Players should generally move to higher-level targets as they are unlocked, provided they can maintain a reasonable success chance. The table below lists pickpocketing targets that provide a useful experience progression. It omits targets that do not improve experience rates, are mainly useful for specific loot or currency, or have lock-out mechanics that make their practical rates route-dependent. Some targets are more practical than their experience rate alone suggests. Menaphite marketeers require partial completion of The Jack of Spades and are a simple early option. Knights of Ardougne are useful Ardougne targets, as they can benefit from the Medium Ardougne achievements success chance boost and have convenient training spots. The hard and elite Ardougne achievements apply the same boost anywhere, including targets outside Ardougne.

The rates below are idealised base rates using 2,000 successful pickpockets per hour and do not include experience boosts, bonus experience, banking, movement, failures, or time spent refreshing buffs. The Sticky Fingers relic increases the rate of auto-pickpocketing, but reduces experience per pickpocket, so experience rates are broadly similar if the player is not interrupted.

At level 62 Thieving, and with the Thieves' Guild capers completed, players can begin safecracking. First speak to the safe-cracking trainer in the Thieves' Guild to receive a stethoscope and a small loot bag if you haven't already.

Begin by cracking safes in Misthalin with level 62 Thieving. Crack open safes by turning their dial. To open safes faster, players should keep an eye on the safe they are opening and wait for it to briefly flash blue or listen for an audio cue. Clicking on the safe again when this occurs will immediately unlock one of the remaining locks on the safe. At this level range you will need to crack three dial locks to open each safe. 405 experience is awarded for unlocking each of the first two dial locks. 1,600 experience is awarded for successfully unlocking a safe. After cracking a safe, fill up your loot bag. The loot can be fenced at the Thieves' Guild with Chief Thief Robin for Thieving experience and pilfer points to spend in Dodgy Derek's Dirty Deals. Uncommon looted special items can be handed in to Darren Lightfinger for 10 pilfer points each. Pilfer points can be used to unlock the following upgrades for safecracking:

Almost all safes around Gielinor take five minutes of in-game time to reset after being unlocked. Hop between locations and keep cracking safes for maximum XP, rather than waiting at an opened safe for it to close. Safecracking provides around 300,000 experience an hour at level 62, with up to 400,000 experience an hour being possible if clicking when the blue flash cue appears.

At level 76 Thieving, players should continue to crack safes, moving to Asgarnia. The most efficient safes to loot are the two in the Black Knights' Fortress (assuming the player owns the Skull of Remembrance for fast teleportation – climb down the staircase and the two safes are in the treasure room west), then the two on the roof of Burthorpe Castle in the equipment room, and finally the two in Port Sarim above the jewellery store and forge. Depending on how attentive you choose to be, you may find that only the first four safes are enough for a 5-minute rotation.

If the Skull of Remembrance is not an option, you should fill out your rotation with some of the four safes in Falador. Using the Mining Guild resource dungeon teleport on a Hoardstalker Ring or Dungeoneering Cape and climbing the ladders will bring you the closest to the Falador safes. The Arc Journal can teleport the player to Quartermaster Gully in Port Sarim, which is close to the Port Sarim safes and requires no charges.

This can provide up to 400,000 experience an hour. Clicking on the safes when they flash blue, for faster experience, you can gain up to 500,000 experience an hour.

At level 83 Thieving, players should continue to crack safes, moving to Kandarin. At higher levels, Thieving proficiency and success (RNG) may, on your route, take you back to a safe that has not been reset yet. In this case, to maximize experience, have a selection of low-level safes to crack in case you encounter this situation. This can provide up to 500,000 experience an hour. Clicking on the safes when they flash blue can give up to 600,000 experience an hour.

At level 90 Thieving, players should incorporate hidden safes into their route, most notably the safes in the Rogues' Castle in the Wilderness. This is up to around 950,000 experience per hour if the player has completed the hard Wilderness achievements. For faster trips, Double Surge and Dive or Bladed Dive are helpful for getting around. The armoured zombie at Zemouregal's fort and rogues in their castle can often be Barged as another movement ability.

The Wilderness safes are prioritised because they give the most experience. The safes in the Wilderness and in Zemouregal's fort have a cooldown of 10 minutes, as opposed to the usual 5 minutes of other safes. Zanaris and Camelot are included to fill out the rotation because all of the special safes would otherwise still be on cooldown. With this, the Wilderness safes and the Zemouregal's fort's safes should be looted every 10 minutes. With 92 or higher Thieving, Abyssal Lurker scrolls can be used to get a +4 boost that will allow the player to loot all four safes in Zemouregal's fort.

Bringing some Thieves' Guild teleport tablets will allow players to quick empty their loot bag without losing much XP. With the medium loot bag, the bag will be filled roughly every two cycles.

At level 95 Thieving, players can begin heists. Heists are active, route- and timing-focused content where players build up loot by stealing from chests/safes and other sources while avoiding guards, traps, and hazards. Experience rates vary depending on completion speed, route choice, and mistakes. Heists award loot points into the stolen goods bag received on entry. The bag holds up to 500 loot points. Upon exiting a heist, stolen goods are removed and Thieving experience and item rewards are granted based on loot obtained. If the heist is exited without looting the relevant rare chest, loot points are halved for experience and rewards. Logging out within a heist resets progress and deletes any loot.

The Vault of Hereditas heist requires level 95 Thieving to access; the requirement is not boostable. The vault is located within a sealed wing of the Kharid-et Dig Site and requires completion of the Breaking the Seal mystery to access. Players must speak to Liara outside the entrance before entering.

See Vault of Hereditas/Strategies for route details and recommended setups. Safes require Thieving to open; the stethoscope or master thief's stethoscope increases safe opening speed. Crevices require Agility and are required for some loot sources/shortcuts. The base experience is 400 per loot; the total loot points available is 535 (with slightly more possible via multiple loot procs). There is a 500-point cap, so not all sources must be looted to reach this. Loot point penalties for being caught/expelled are reduced by the Thieving master cape perk.

At level 95, players can earn roughly 180,000 base experience per run, equivalent to about 1,200,000–1,350,000 experience per hour if completing runs in 8–9 minutes. When incorporating safes at level 98 with boosting, players can earn roughly 315,000 base experience per run, equivalent to about 1,900,000 experience per hour if completing runs in 10 minutes.

The Asuran Arsenal is a heist requiring level 108 Thieving to access; the requirement is not boostable. It is located on the far south-east shore of Anachronia in the Swamp Fortress. Players must speak to Liara outside the entrance to unlock it. Unlike the Vault of Hereditas heist, the Asuran Arsenal contains traps and hazards that can cause damage as well as a loss of loot. Logging out or dying will reset progress and delete any loot; deaths here are unsafe.

See Asuran Arsenal/Strategies for route details and recommended setups. Safes require Thieving to open; the stethoscope or master thief's stethoscope increases safe opening speed. Rubble, crevices, and the railing require Agility, Agility, and Agility respectively, and are required for some loot sources/shortcuts. The base experience is 450 per loot. Total loot points available is 625; omitting the optional and side rooms can still reach 505 points (cap with minimal additional looting/backtracking).

At level 108, players can earn roughly 230,000 base experience per run, equivalent to about 1,600,000 xp/hr if completing runs in 8.5–9 minutes. When incorporating safes at level 110 with boosting, players can earn roughly 340,000 base experience per run, equivalent to about 2,260,000 experience per hour if completing runs in 9 minutes.

For a low-intensity training method you may wish to continue pickpocketing NPCs, progressing to higher level targets as you level up. You will continually pickpocket an NPC until you are caught or until your inventory becomes full. Success chance for pickpocketing is based on the player's Thieving level compared with the target's level requirement, with an opening success boost for a limited number of pickpockets. After those boosted pickpockets, the success chance gradually falls until the player is caught or the pickpocketing chain is reset. Changing target or refreshing Crystal Mask resets the chain. The Thieving chance calculator can be used to check success chance, AFK duration, experience, and profit for a specific setup. With higher Agility levels you may loot an NPC multiple times; this gives additional loot but no additional Thieving experience.

In general, players should move to the highest-level target that they can pickpocket comfortably. Lower-level targets may still be preferable where they have simpler loot, less movement, or better access to success chance boosts. The table below lists pickpocketing targets that provide a useful experience progression. It omits targets that do not improve experience rates, are mainly useful for specific loot or currency, or have lock-out mechanics that make their practical rates route-dependent. The listed rates assume 2,000 uninterrupted successful pickpockets per hour, with no experience boosts, bonus experience, banking, movement, failures, or time spent refreshing buffs.

Players can do a Thieving performance at the Circus Distraction and Diversion once per week if they have completed the Some Like It Cold quest. To enter the circus the player must gain a circus ticket from the ticket vendor, which is randomly located in one of 12 possible locations each week. Players can start their Thieving performance by standing on the star next to Teddy.

During the performance players have 5 attempts to perform up to 5 different tricks. Thieving experience is received upon the first successful attempt of each trick that the player performs: repeating a trick more than once does not grant additional experience. Each trick has a recommended Thieving level to attempt; however this level is not required in order to perform the trick, as it is possible to successfully perform or fail to perform a trick at any Thieving level. It may take several attempts for a trick is successfully performed. However, when a player performs a trick that has a higher recommended Thieving level than they currently have, the experience received will be the same as that given for performing a trick with half the recommended Thieving level, rounded down.

To gain the most experience from the Thieving performance players should begin by performing the highest recommended level trick for their current Thieving level, and work down to the trick with a recommended level half of their current Thieving level. After this players should perform any tricks with a recommended Thieving level which is greater than their current Thieving level and then finally perform any tricks with a recommended level of less than half of their current Thieving level. The Distraction and Diversion's interface will display the recommended Thieving level for the performance's tricks, as well as show which tricks the player has performed successfully. Players can receive a total of 14,260 experience, in about 45 seconds, if they successfully perform all 5 tricks with level 90 Thieving or higher. With completion of the Back to the Freezer quest players may gain up to 1.5 times as much experience from each trick, at level 99.
